findings.description:
The new scrubber can remove destructive commands from a heredoc that is executed later in the same Bash invocation. For example: `tee /tmp/payload <<'EOF'
printf '%s
' "$(rm -rf /)"
EOF
bash -c 'source /tmp/payload; :'`. `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` compares complete token basenames with `payload`; the quoted shell-program token instead has basename `payload; :`, so execution is missed. The quoted heredoc's printf line is then discarded.
findings.failure_mode: The fence receives scrubbed text without `rm -rf /` and permits the invocation, while Bash subsequently sources the file and executes the destructive substitution. Previously, the quoted-cat scrub did not remove this tee heredoc.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat later interpreter or wrapper invocations containing a destination reference as executable even when the reference occurs inside a quoted program argument. When execution cannot be ruled out, preserve the entire heredoc body for scanning. Add this invocation to the fence regression corpus.

findings.description: read_position treats the run position as known whenever sprint-plan-state.json has a fresh derived_at. It never checks timestamps.last_activity. check_implementation_active does check it and refuses the sanction when the activity stamp is missing or older than 24 h. So a cache with state RUNNING, a fresh derived_at and a stale or absent last_activity gets no sanction, while read_position still calls the position known.
findings.failure_mode: Under implement_gate.mode: deny, every App Zone write during a live RUNNING sprint is denied. The deny reason says 'derived position: RUNNING', which contradicts itself. This happens whenever run-checkpoint.sh derive refreshes derived_at without restamping last_activity.
findings.suggested_fix: Make read_position and check_implementation_active agree. A RUNNING state with a fresh derived_at should be sanctioned, or should be treated as an unknown position that falls back to ask. Also add a bats case for RUNNING with fresh derived_at and stale last_activity under deny.

findings.description: The marker sanction expires 7200 s after started_at. Nothing in the gate refreshes it, so an /implement or /bug session longer than two hours loses the sanction partway through. It then logs stale_marker on every write.
findings.failure_mode: Under deny with a known non-RUNNING position, writes partway through a long implementation are refused. Under ask, the operator starts getting prompts on every write, and an unattended session stalls.
findings.suggested_fix: Have run-checkpoint.sh refresh the marker, for example on record-round or a heartbeat. Or measure freshness from a last-touched field, and make the window configurable.

findings.description: The header calls the model-authored claim tighten-only, meaning it can never grant an allow. But the new marker sanction does grant an allow, and the model itself creates the marker by running run-checkpoint.sh mark through Bash. The Write/Edit trust-input check on .run/implement-active.json does not apply to that path. Under deny, the fence therefore depends on the model choosing not to mark.
findings.failure_mode: The opt-in deny mode does not actually stop an agent that wants to write outside a run. The agent can sanction itself before writing, which undercuts the main property deny is supposed to provide.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the marker as advisory-grade. Alternatively, require the marker to match the derived sprint position, for example the marker's sprint must equal the current sprint in sprint-plan-state.json, so that it cannot sanction writes on its own.

findings.description: is_enforcement_enabled no longer reads $CONFIG_FILE. loa_knob resolves its own config path. The loa-l7-surface-soul.sh hook in the same diff passes LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE when its config differs, but this script does not. The default also changes: with no config file or no key, enforcement used to be on and is now off, because the standard profile reads false.
findings.failure_mode: Two cases go wrong. A caller that points CONFIG_FILE at another config with enforce: true is silently ignored. Projects with no .loa.config.yaml lose danger-level enforcement with no warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the config path through, using LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CONFIG_FILE" loa_knob .... Also log a one-time notice when enforcement is off only because of the profile default.

findings.description: If sourcing profile-lib.sh fails, the && chain skips the assignment and `enabled` keeps whatever value it had before. The old code always assigned it. loa-l6-surface-handoffs.sh and loa-l7-surface-soul.sh set enabled="false" first. loa-kf-surface.sh and loa-decisions-surface.sh do not.
findings.failure_mode: Suppose the profile lib is missing or broken, for example on a partial framework update. If the variable is unset under set -u, the session-start hook aborts. Otherwise it acts on a stale value.
findings.suggested_fix: Set enabled="false" before the source line in both hooks, as the l6 and l7 hooks already do.

findings.description: The new _ig_derived_ok check also applies in the default ask mode. A RUNNING cache whose derived_at is older than run_mode.stale_hours, default 12, now loses its sanction even when last_activity is fresh. The header still says ask mode behaves exactly as before. _ig_within also fails for timestamps with a numeric offset such as +00:00, because only fractional-Z forms are normalized.
findings.failure_mode: Overnight sprint-plan runs that are not re-derived within 12 h start getting asks on App Zone writes, which stalls autonomous runs. The same happens to any derived_at written with an offset.
findings.suggested_fix: Check that run-checkpoint.sh restamps derived_at at every checkpoint and always writes it as UTC Z. Also normalize offsets in _ig_within, or apply the derived_at bound only under deny.

findings.cross_file_justification: Removing the C-TEAM entries deletes the generated Agent Teams table from CLAUDE.loa.md. Other generators and validators, such as generate-constraints.sh, validate-constraints.sh and agent-teams-reference.md, may still reference that category or section marker.
findings.description: Five MUST constraints for teammates are removed together with the instructions generated from them. Only C-TEAM-001 and C-TEAM-005 were described as hook-enforced. C-TEAM-002, 003 and 004 cover beads, .run state files and git commit/push, and existed only as instructions.
findings.failure_mode: In agent-team sessions, teammates no longer get the single-writer rules for beads SQLite, state files and the git index. Concurrent writes can cause lock contention or lost updates, and the hooks do not stop them.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm that the hooks now enforce 002 through 004, or that the rules moved to agent-teams-reference.md. Otherwise keep those three rows in the generated block.
